🌎 BEYOND THE 956

WINTER HAVEN, Fla. — The Polk County Sheriff's Office arrested 281 people in a seven-day undercover operation targeting alleged child predators, prostitution and human trafficking, Sheriff Grady Judd announced October 30. The operation, dubbed “Polk Around and Find Out II,” was described as the largest undercover investigation in the department's history.

Of the 281 arrests, 31 were tied to alleged child predators — people accused of communicating online with someone they believed to be a child, or with a child's guardian, and in some cases traveling to an undercover location expecting to meet a minor. Another 239 arrests were tied to prostitution-related offenses, and 11 were classified as other arrests. Those arrested face a combined 488 charges, including 198 felonies.

Seventeen of those arrested told detectives they work at local theme parks or resorts, the Sheriff's Office said. Sheriff Judd said 13 worked for Disney and four for Universal Studios, and that Disney had told investigators the employees had been fired. Seven of the theme park or resort workers were among those arrested in the child-predator portion of the investigation, according to reports on the Sheriff's Office announcement.

Investigators also identified 11 potential human trafficking victims during the operation and offered them assistance through social service organizations, according to reports.

Everyone arrested has only been charged, not convicted. The charges are allegations, and all of those arrested are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post; Polk County Sheriff's Office, via USA TODAY and WKMG News 6 reports.
